summary: Verified the r3 bundle end to end from the tar bytes (SHA-256 matches the review digest). Every headline claim reproduces: 39 DAG nodes in 39 dependency-consistent single-task waves (fixed serial order), 118 required checks (108 retained + 10 repair, all required), 92 acceptance IDs covered bijectively by checks and the aggregation table, three journeys with execution_owner=VERIFY, amendment 3 (llmwiki projectization + Docker terminal channel with receipts and honest sandbox-EPERM disclosure), and both r2 codex fixes present and mutually consistent (journey_execution.order_semantics forbidding retrofitted recovery windows; V_RW expected defined as a fault window within the same product Run before completed, cross-referenced from V_SAME_RUN_DELIVERY). All four drift-lock anchors reproduce from bundle bytes, including the plan digest under the declared checkbox-normalized-v1 mode. Ownership/allowed-path mapping is exact across all 39 nodes. Remaining weaknesses are minor bookkeeping, not architecture: the after_hashes refresh covers only the four locked artifacts (design.md diverges between replan-record.before_hashes and spec-baseline.sources with no amendment noting the change; execution-prompt.md/HANDOFF.md lack after-state entries), and the drift-lock amendment-3 wording compresses 'dag/contract 零改动' with 'contract hash 相应更新' into one record. No blocking findings; I would authorize the gated next step (implementation dispatch under this plan).
